tagline.text: A Davao farm resort with a chocolate museum and butterfly and bird gardens

location.label: Location
location.text: Malagos, Baguio District, Davao City (toward Calinan)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (March–May is easiest for outdoor activities)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱400~1,500 (admission, transport and meals, per person for a day trip)

children.text: Malagos Garden Resort is a farm-based attraction in Malagos on the outskirts of Davao City that opened in 1994. With the first chocolate museum in the Philippines, a butterfly garden, a bird feeding dome and garden paths, it suits family trips and half-day outings.

Malagos Garden Resort is an agri-ecotourism site in Malagos, Baguio District, Davao City. According to Wikipedia it opened in 1994 and is run by the Puentespina family. About 12 hectares (30 acres) are used for tourism and accredited as a farm tourism site by the Department of Tourism, and a separate cacao farm of about 70 hectares (170 acres) is operated. It is described as about 40 minutes by car from downtown Davao, which makes it a good day trip.

What made Malagos famous is chocolate. The family began making Malagos Chocolate in Davao in 2012, and the first chocolate museum in the Philippines is inside this resort. The opening date differs by source: Wikipedia says November 2016, while the museum's official site says March 8, 2017. Through infographics, video and interactive displays, the museum explains how cacao becomes chocolate, and in the chocolate laboratory you can make your own.

There are also a butterfly garden and butterfly museum, a bird feeding dome, a place to see small animals, and walking paths and a lagoon. Wikipedia also mentions an orchid farm, a children's playground, a skate park and an outdoor theater. One guide tells visitors to check separately whether all these activities are included in admission. Admission and extra charges differ between sources, so confirm just before you go.

Operations have changed over time. Wikipedia says the resort stopped admitting tourists in mid-March 2020 because of COVID-19. The official site, on the other hand, promotes a bird show that has run for nearly 25 years and says the museum is open daily. Because Wikipedia describes the bird show as a weekend performance until 2019, you need to check directly with official channels for the current bird show schedule and whether advance booking is required.

This chocolate museum is presented as the first in the Philippines. The official site says it has four parts: a museum section, an interactive zone, a chocolate bar and a chocolate laboratory. The museum is described as open without a reservation, daily from 8 AM to 5 PM.

A guided walking tour that follows the process from cacao tree to chocolate bar and takes about 1 to 1.5 hours. It runs twice a day (10 AM and 1 PM) from Monday to Saturday and is closed on Sundays and holidays. Advance booking by email is required.
There is a garden and museum explaining the life stages of butterflies. Some zones are meant to be kept quiet, so follow the instructions.
You can walk into the dome and feed native and exotic birds. It is a good stop to enjoy with children.
There are paths lined with tropical flowers and a lagoon, and boat rides are reportedly available. It is hot at midday, so walk in the morning or late afternoon.
The official site promotes an interactive bird show for wildlife education. One review says weekend prices include the bird show. Schedules and prices vary by season, so confirm them.
Activities such as calesa rides, horseback riding, pizza making, chocolate making, tree planting and feeding koi are listed. Check on site which ones cost extra.
There are restaurants said to use farm-grown vegetables and local ingredients, plus Koi Cafe and Viewdeck Cafe. Menus such as cheese and chocolate pairing are recommended.

items.title: Day trip from Davao
items.subtitle: Morning arrival, focused on the museum and gardens

children.text: Leave downtown Davao for Malagos. It is described as about 40 minutes by car.
Pay admission and start with the chocolate museum. The museum opens at 8 AM.
Tour the butterfly garden and the bird feeding dome.
Have lunch at a farm restaurant or cafe. Outside food is reportedly not allowed.
Stroll the garden and lagoon and choose an activity such as a calesa ride or horseback riding.
Buy souvenirs at the chocolate shop.
Leave early and head back to Davao. Official operating hours are described as ending around 5 PM.
To fit in the Tree-to-Bar experience, plan around 10 AM or 1 PM Monday to Saturday and book in advance. The bird show is described as weekend-focused, so check the schedule if you visit on a weekend.

items.title: Two days, one night at the resort
items.subtitle: Book a room and take it easy

children.text: Arrive, check in and tour the museum and gardens.
Have dinner at Koi Cafe, which is described as serving dinner.
On the second morning, have breakfast early at Koi Cafe, then take a walk or go birdwatching.
Check out and return to Davao.
According to a 2023 guide, a Deluxe Room cost about ₱5,800 for two people. Check current rates with the official reservation office.

items.title: By plane from Manila to Davao

children.text: Domestic flights run daily from Manila (MNL) to Davao (DVO). Duration and flights vary by airline and season, so check on a booking site.

items.title: Rental car or taxi from Davao

children.text: It is described as about 40 minutes by car from downtown Davao. One travel service lists about 38.9 km and roughly an hour by car from the airport. It varies with traffic.
A rental car or a car with a driver is convenient. Public transport may be scarce on the way back from the Calinan side, so allow extra time.
One guide tells you to go from Davao to Bankerohan Terminal and take a jeepney or bus to Calinan. Calinan is said to take 45–60 minutes.

From Calinan to the resort, a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) takes 10–15 minutes and a tricycle for groups takes 15–20 minutes. Some jeepneys reportedly drop you near the entrance. Check fares locally.

The gardens and outdoor facilities are the main draw, so drier periods are more comfortable for walking. One guide recommends visiting in the morning or late afternoon, when it is cooler and the animals are more active. Weekdays are said to be quieter.
Davao has no sharp wet and dry seasons and is humid year-round. Bring an umbrella or poncho for showers, and a hat and sunscreen for midday.
The bird show is described as weekend-focused, so go on a weekend if you want to see it. Weekends are busier and prices are higher.

The chocolate museum is an indoor attraction you can enjoy even in the rain, so it is a fallback on uncertain days. In contrast, the butterfly garden, bird feeding dome and walking paths are more rewarding on clear days. To see everything, we suggest outdoor sights on a clear morning and the museum during the hot midday or when it rains.

The resort has rooms, so you can stay overnight. According to a 2023 guide, a Deluxe Room was about ₱5,800 for two, a Honeymoon Suite about ₱8,500 for two and a Family Suite about ₱10,800 for four. Check current rates and booking conditions with the official reservation office. Staying in the city and visiting as a day trip is more economical.

The official site lists Koi Cafe, which serves breakfast and dinner, Viewdeck Cafe, open during the day (10 AM–5 PM), and the Corral Pavilion, which hosts the weekend lunch buffet. Bringing outside food and drinks is reportedly not allowed. Malagos chocolate is popular as a souvenir, and the cheese and chocolate pairing is also recommended.

According to Wikipedia, a chocolate spa using cacao husks opened in June 2018. One guide lists prices such as ₱600 for a 30-minute head and shoulder massage, ₱1,100 for a one-hour signature massage and ₱1,200 for a one-hour cacao facial. These are 2023 figures and whether the spa is currently operating needs checking, so ask for the price again when you book.
Before you go, contact the resort (malagos.com, reservation email) to check admission prices, the bird show schedule and whether advance booking is needed.
Going in the morning or late afternoon means it is not too hot and the animals are active.
Bring comfortable shoes, a hat, sunscreen, water and binoculars. An umbrella is also useful in the rainy season.
Chocolate making and the Tree-to-Bar experience may need reservations, so ask ahead.
In quiet zones such as the butterfly garden, keep your voice low and do not feed the animals carelessly.
Bring cash or a card to buy chocolate and souvenirs.
During the COVID period, masks, a booking confirmation and ID were required. Ask whether the same rules apply now.
For a day trip, arrange your return transport in advance. Public transport may stop running early.
If you travel with children, check the child price bracket (ages 4–11) and keep a guardian beside small children in quiet zones such as the butterfly garden.
Prices, operating hours and the bird show schedule differ between sources. There were periods when advance booking was required, so always check official channels before you visit.
During the COVID period, advance booking was mandatory and walk-in entry was restricted. Check the current rules.
Outside food and drinks are reportedly not allowed.
Do not feed or disturb the animals without staff permission.
The pool is reportedly for in-house guests only, so check if swimming is your goal.
When coming by public transport, check the last transport time from Calinan.
